perf.summary: The trial-division loop uses 'd*d <= currentN' and a separate '%' then '/'; combine and strength-reduce, and reuse the quotient to avoid a redundant division.
perf.currentCost: Each candidate d does a multiply (d*d) for the bound, a modulo (currentN % d), and on a hit a separate division (currentN / d) — i.e. a divide plus a separate modulo (two expensive 64-bit div ops) for divisors that hit.
perf.proposedChange: Compute long q = currentN / d; long r = currentN - q*d; once per d (single div + mul-sub gives both quotient and remainder), test r==0, and pass q directly into the recursive call. Keep d*d bound or precompute the loop limit via an integer sqrt to avoid the per-iteration multiply.
perf.rationale: 64-bit integer division is the dominant cost; fusing div+mod into one division plus a multiply-subtract removes one full divide on every successful factor, and reusing q removes the second division in the recursion argument. Optionally hoisting an isqrt bound removes the per-iteration multiply.
perf.risk: currentN and d are positive here (n>1, minFactor>=2), so q*d cannot overflow within range and r==0 test is exact. Pure refactor preserving outputs and traversal order.
